pages.title: Two views
pages.summary: Contrasts empirical robustness, measured by attacking the model, with certified robustness, proved for a radius.

terms.definition: Robustness measured by running attacks against the model and reporting what it survives.
terms.intuition: Cheap and optimistic: it says the attacks you tried failed, which a better attack can undo tomorrow.
terms.inThisCourse: The left column of this slide, set against the certified column.

terms.definition: Robustness proved for a radius: no perturbation inside it can change the prediction.
terms.intuition: Expensive and pessimistic, but the number cannot be taken away by a smarter attack later.
terms.inThisCourse: The right column of this slide; what randomized smoothing delivers.

terms.definition: The size of the region around an input inside which no perturbation can change the smoothed prediction.
terms.intuition: It is the number the whole method exists to produce: how far an attacker may move before the guarantee stops.
terms.inThisCourse: Described here as the thing no attack can cross, at the cost of smaller reported numbers.

passages.text: Empirical Attack the model and report what survives. Cheap to run, easy to break later.
passages.explanation: The empirical column evaluates a defense by attacking it and reporting the accuracy that remains. It is cheap, and its number is only as strong as the attacks that were tried.

passages.text: Certified Prove a radius no attack can cross. Expensive, smaller numbers, but honest.
passages.explanation: The certified column proves a radius instead of testing one. The computation costs more and the reported accuracy is lower, but no future attack can invalidate it.

pages.summary: A placeholder page: four ordering sentences with no lecture content.

pages.title: Summary
pages.summary: Recaps the trade-off: the guarantee is bought with accuracy, which is why certified numbers look small.

terms.definition: A defense that comes with a proof that no perturbation inside a stated radius can change the model's prediction. The proof holds against every attack in that radius, not only the ones that were tried.
terms.intuition: It replaces the arms race of attack and patch with a guarantee you can state once and rely on.
terms.inThisCourse: Closed here on its cost: the guarantee is paid for in accuracy.

terms.definition: The size of the region around an input inside which no perturbation can change the smoothed prediction.
terms.intuition: It is the number the whole method exists to produce: how far an attacker may move before the guarantee stops.
terms.inThisCourse: The scope of the guarantee: every attack inside the radius, none outside it.

passages.text: Certified defenses trade accuracy for a guarantee that holds against every attack inside the radius, so the numbers look small.
passages.explanation: A certified model gives up clean accuracy in exchange for a proof. The proof covers every perturbation inside the radius, which is why its reported accuracy is lower than an empirical one.
